[[No overall control]] | after_election = | after_party = }} The '''2026 Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council election''' was held on 7 May 2026 to elect members to [[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] in [[Hertfordshire]], [[England]], taking place on the same day as other [[2026 United Kingdom local elections|local elections]].{{cite web |title=Election Day – Thursday 7 May 2026 |url=https://www.welhat.gov.uk/voting-elections/election-day-thursday-7-may-2026/1 |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=31 March 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Mountney |first1=Dan |title=2026 local elections to go ahead after government u-turn |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25859231.2026-local-elections-go-ahead-government-u-turn/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=16 February 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Wheeler |first1=Richard |title=Government abandons plans to delay 30 council elections |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c70ne31d884o |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=16 February 2026}} 16 of the council's 48 seats were up for election, with an additional 17th seat being contested in Welwyn East due to a [[by-election]]. The election was originally cancelled in January 2026 in preparation for [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|structural changes to local government]], however, the [[Starmer ministry|government]] reversed its decision the following month.{{cite web |last1=Barrow |first1=Georgia |title=Welwyn Hatfield council election among 29 postponed |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25788048.welwyn-hatfield-council-election-among-29-postponed/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=22 January 2026}} This election was the last held in Welwyn Hatfield before local government reorganisation. While most of the seats contested were held by their original parties, [[Reform UK|Reform]] won three seats, joining the Council for the first time. This included winning the Hollybush ward, the seat of the Mayor, Lynn Chesterman. The [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] lost both their incumbent seats, meaning they were no longer represented in the Council.{{cite web | last=Coyle | first=Simon | title=Welwyn Hatfield local election results 2026 in full | website=Manchester Evening News | date=8 May 2026 | url=https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/uk-news/welwyn-hatfield-local-election-results-33869062|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20260509173226/https://www.manchestereveningnews.co.uk/news/uk-news/welwyn-hatfield-local-election-results-33869062|archive-date=9 May 2026|url-status=live | access-date=9 May 2026}} ==Background== In the [[2024 Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council election|2024 local elections]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] won 8 seats while the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] and [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] won 4 seats each, maintaining [[no overall control]] of the council.{{cite web |title=Election Results 2 May 2024 |url=https://www.welhat.gov.uk/voting-elections/election-results-2-may-2024 |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=3 May 2024}} The Liberal Democrats and Labour had formed a [[Coalition government|coalition]] after the [[2023 Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council election|2023 election]], though, following the 2024 election, Labour overtook the Liberal Democrats and became the main party in the coalition, with Labour councillor Max Holloway of Howlands being appointed [[Executive arrangements#Leader and cabinet|leader of the council]].{{cite web |last1=Mountney |first1=Dan |title=New Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council leader announced |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/24324709.new-welwyn-hatfield-borough-council-leader-announced/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=16 May 2024}} In the [[2024 United Kingdom general election|2024 general election]], the constituency of [[Welwyn Hatfield (UK Parliament constituency)|Welwyn Hatfield]] was won by the Labour Party candidate [[Andrew Lewin]], who unseated [[Secretary of State for Defence|defence secretary]] and 19-year Conservative incumbent [[Grant Shapps]], while the [[Hertsmere (UK Parliament constituency)|Hertsmere]] constituency (which includes the [[Northaw and Cuffley]] ward of Welwyn Hatfield borough) was held by Conservative [[Oliver Dowden]], the former [[Deputy Prime Minister of the United Kingdom|deputy prime minister]] under [[Rishi Sunak]].{{cite web |title=Welwyn Hatfield – General election results 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/uk/constituencies/E14001573 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=5 July 2024}}{{cite web |title=Broxbourne – General election results 2024 |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/election/2024/uk/constituencies/E14001139 |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=5 July 2024}} There were two [[by-election]]s held between the 2024 and 2026 elections, both held in conjunction with the [[2025 Hertfordshire County Council January 2025, councillor Sunny Thusu of Welwyn West was suspended from the [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] after it was revealed that he had cheated on his [[Medical school in the United Kingdom|medical school]] exams in 2023.{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Welwyn Hatfield councillor and NHS surgeon cheated on exams |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/24846977.welwyn-hatfield-councillor-nhs-surgeon-cheated-exams/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=10 January 2026}} He subsequently sat as an [[Independent politician|independent]], though his suspension was lifted in June 2025.{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Disgraced doctor readmitted to Welwyn Hatfield Conservative group |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25221546.disgraced-doctor-readmitted-welwyn-hatfield-conservative-group/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=7 June 2025}} In May 2025, councillor Larry Crofton of Hatfield East left the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] and joined the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]], citing disagreements with the [[Starmer ministry|national Labour government]].{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Welwyn Hatfield Labour councillor defects to Greens |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25156833.welwyn-hatfield-labour-councillor-defects-greens/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=12 May 2025}} In August 2025, councillor Jill Weston of Howlands left Labour to sit as an [[Independent politician|independent]] after disagreements over the Labour government's position on the [[Gaza war]].{{cite web |last1=McEvoy |first1=Louise |title=Welwyn Hatfield councillor resigns over Gaza genocide |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25416174.welwyn-hatfield-councillor-resigns-gaza-genocide/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=26 August 2025}} In January 2026, councillor Lucy Musk of Haldens left Labour and joined the Green Party over disagreements with [[Keir Starmer]]'s Labour government.{{cite web |last1=Makar |first1=Samuel |title=Welwyn Hatfield: Haldens councillor defects to Greens |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25757374.welwyn-hatfield-haldens-councillor-defects-greens/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=12 January 2026}} That month, Conservative councillor Roger Trigg of Welwyn East died, leaving the seat vacant.{{cite web |title=Statement on the passing of Councillor Roger Trigg |url=https://one.welhat.gov.uk/news/article/441/statement-on-the-passing-of-councillor-roger-trigg |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=26 January 2026}} On 15 January 2026, the council held a [[Non-binding resolution|non-binding vote]] on whether to cancel the 2026 elections in preparation for [[Upcoming structural changes to local government in England|local government reorganisaton]], with a binding cabinet vote after the full council meeting.{{cite web |last1=Holloway |first1=Max |last2=Quinton |first2=Jane |title=Statement from Leader and Deputy Leader of Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council on May 2026 Local Elections |url=https://one.welhat.gov.uk/news/article/434/statement-from-leader-and-deputy-leader-of-welwyn-hatfield-borough-council-on-may-2026-local-elections |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=5 January 2026}} The full council voted 24–15 against cancellation, but the cabinet voted 4–3 for cancellation, with the Labour councillors in the cabinet voting for and the Liberal Democrat councillors voting against.{{cite web |title=Special Council – Thursday 15th January 2026 printed minutes |url=https://democracy.welhat.gov.uk/documents/g2004/Printed%20minutes%2015th-Jan-2026%2018.00%20Council.pdf |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |format=PDF |date=15 January 2026}}{{cite web |title=Special Cabinet – Thursday 15th January 2026 printed minutes |url=https://democracy.welhat.gov.uk/documents/g2006/Printed%20minutes%2015th-Jan-2026%2021.00%20Cabinet.pdf |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |format=PDF |date=15 January 2026}} Following the cabinet vote, the Liberal Democrats withdrew from their [[Coalition government|coalition agreement]] with Labour, with Liberal Democrat leader Jane Quinton accusing Labour of a "betrayal of democracy".{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Coalition embroiled in public row over election postponement |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25772065.coalition-embroiled-public-row-election-postponement/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=16 January 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Welwyn Hatfield Lib Dems trigger process to end coalition |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25780173.welwyn-hatfield-lib-dems-trigger-process-end-coalition/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=20 January 2026}} The election was formally cancelled by [[Steve Reed (politician)|Steve Reed]], the [[Secretary of State for Housing, Communities and Local Government|secretary of state for local government]], on 22 January.{{cite web |last1=McKiernan |first1=Jennifer |last2=Forsyth |first2=Alex |title=Thirty English councils to delay elections, minister confirms |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/cx2ggk333l4o |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=22 January 2026}} On 29 January, following criticism from other parties, Labour leader of the council Max Holloway of Howlands announced he would be standing down as leader on 6 February, when a new leader would be elected.{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Council leader resigns after election postponement |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c8d0274zngeo |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=29 January 2026}}{{cite web |last1=Mountney |first1=Dan |title=Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council leader announces resignation |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25807325.welwyn-hatfield-borough-council-leader-announces-resignation/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=29 January 2026}} In February 2026, Labour councillor Rose Grewal of Hatfield Villages was elected as the new leader of the council to replace Holloway, with a tentative new coalition agreement with the Liberal Democrats in the final stages of negotiation.{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=New council leader elected after reorganisation row |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/articles/c5yv8n40dw2o |publisher=[[BBC News]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=10 February 2026}} That same month, the government announced that all cancelled elections in England, including Welwyn Hatfield, were to go ahead following a legal challenge by [[Reform UK]]. On 16 February, councillor Jane Quinton of Panshanger announced that she would be standing down as deputy leader of the council and leader of the council's Liberal Democrat group.{{cite web |last1=Day |first1=Christopher |title=Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council’s deputy leader stands down |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25861463.welwyn-hatfield-borough-councils-deputy-leader-stands/ |publisher=Welwyn Hatfield Times |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=17 January 2026}} She was replaced in both roles by councillor Sandreni Bonfante of Welham Green and Hatfield South.{{cite web |title=Changes to Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council’s Cabinet Confirmed |url=https://one.welhat.gov.uk/news/article/451/changes-to-welwyn-hatfield-borough-council-s-cabinet-confirmed |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=17 February 2026 |date=16 February 2026}} In March 2026, councillor Russ Platt of Peartree left the Liberal Democrats to sit as an independent, stating that he could not "sit comfortably" in a joint administration with Labour following their attempted cancellation of the May elections.{{Cite web |date=3 March 2026 |title=Lib Dem councillor leaves group and will sit as independent |url=https://www.whtimes.co.uk/news/25904724.welwyn-hatfield-borough-council-liberal-democrat-leaves-group/ |access-date=4 March 2026 |website=Welwyn Hatfield Times |language=en}} ===Previous council composition=== {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After [[2024 Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council election|2024 election]] ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election{{cite web |title=Your Councillors by Party |url=https://democracy.welhat.gov.uk/mgMemberIndex.aspx?FN=PARTY&VW=LIST&PIC=0 |publisher=[[Welwyn Hatfield|Welwyn Hatfield Borough Council]] |access-date=16 February 2026 |date=16 February 2026}} |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
